meta.title: Epic's MCP vs Aethyr · Aethyr docs
meta.description: Every toolset in Epic's UE 5.8 MCP plugin next to the matching Aethyr tool, where Aethyr fills gaps, and where Epic leads.

article.heading: Epic's tools, Aethyr's tools.
article.lead: What Epic's MCP plugin covers in Unreal Engine 5.8, what Aethyr covers, where they overlap, and how Aethyr works around Epic's rough edges.

sections.heading: Two servers, one connection
sections.html:
Unreal Engine 5.8 ships Epic's own MCP plugin, ModelContextProtocol, plus a set of toolset plugins that give it things to do. Aethyr is a separate MCP server with its own tools. This page puts the two side by side. It lists every toolset Epic has, shows which Aethyr tool does the same job, and says plainly where each side leads.

The two aren't rivals you have to pick between. Aethyr bridges Epic's tools through three of its own: epic_list_toolsets, epic_describe_toolset and epic_call_tool. Your AI connects to one server and can reach both sets. The overview in Get Started covers setup. This page goes deeper on the differences.

Numbers on this page are from source. Epic's plugin is experimental in 5.8 and its toolset list will change. At time of writing, the installed 5.8 plugins hold 872 functions across 56 toolset classes. The counts come from reading the source: C++ functions marked AICallable and Python functions decorated with tool_call. Aethyr's own catalog lists 308 native tools across 28 categories at time of writing.

sections.heading: Epic's rough edges and how Aethyr handles them
sections.html:
These are the rough edges you hit with Epic's server on its own and what Aethyr does about each. Some come from the plugin being experimental. Others come from the design, since Epic built a broad, native editor surface and left the safety layer to the client.

AreaEpic's MCP on its ownHow Aethyr handles it
Editor neededThe server lives inside the editor process. With no editor open there are no tools.Aethyr's own tools don't need an editor. The default backend uses your live editor when one is open and starts a headless editor when none is. A mock backend runs with no engine at all for trying the wire format. Note: the bridged Epic tools still need a live editor, because the headless editor never serves them.
Crash isolationThe server runs in-process and speaks HTTP. A tool that goes wrong does so inside your editor.Aethyr's MCP server is a separate executable that talks to the editor plugin over a local socket. A fault in the server doesn't take your editor with it. Note: when a live editor handles a call, the Aethyr plugin still does that work inside the editor.
Server startbAutoStartServer is off by default. Enable the plugin and you get a server that never starts.Aethyr's editor module starts the server when the editor loads. It skips commandlets, a server Epic already started, and a port that's already listening. AETHYR_EPIC_AUTOSTART=0 turns that off. A Blueprint-only project on the precompiled zip can't pick up the optional plugin dependency. For that case, setup writes Saved/Aethyr/Launch-Editor.bat and you start the editor with it.
Toolsets onEvery toolset is its own plugin. A fresh editor only has the ones you enabled.Aethyr's plugin lists ModelContextProtocol and EditorToolset as optional, editor-only dependencies. That brings EditorToolset in by default. AethyrMcp.exe launch-editor --epic-toolsets all starts the editor with every plugin that depends on ToolsetRegistry. It first checks Epic's plugin binaries against your engine's BuildId and refuses with a clear message if they're missing or stale.
Tool SearchWith Tool Search on (the default), the server shows three tools: list_toolsets, describe_toolset and call_tool. With it off, every toolset tool becomes its own MCP tool.The bridge relies on the three-tool form. If it can't find them, its three tools fail with a message that names the plugin, the server and Enable Tool Search as the things to check.
SessionsProbing the server by hand needs an initialize call first. After that, every call needs the Mcp-Session-Id header it returned. Skip it and tools/list answers 400.The bridge does that for you.
Port changesThe server listens on 127.0.0.1:8000/mcp by default. You can change the port and path in project settings.The bridge reads the port and path from your project's settings and falls back to Epic's default. AETHYR_EPIC_URL overrides all three. doctor prints the address that won. Use it to confirm the bridge followed a change.
Read-only modeEpic's settings have allow and block lists for toolset names. They have no read-only switch.Aethyr sorts every Epic tool into read or write. An unknown shape counts as a write. A read-only session (AETHYR_READ_ONLY=1) refuses bridged writes the same way it refuses native ones.
Overlapping callsTool calls run one at a time on the editor's game thread. Nothing on Epic's side coordinates two clients working on the same project.Bridged calls queue behind the same per-project lock as native calls. One session's call can't land in the middle of another session's batch.
Write safetySingle calls apply directly. execute_tool_script can run many calls inside one editor transaction that's undone if the script raises. That's in-editor undo. Nothing in the toolset source checks a compile result before a save or copies the file first.Native writes compile before they save. Aethyr copies each asset to a backup ring before its first save of a session. A batch with atomic:true reverts every change if any step fails. preview_ops dry-runs one first. Bridged writes don't get any of that. Set AETHYR_EPIC_BACKUP=1 and pass target_asset to epic_call_tool to get a backup copy before the call goes out. It's on by default in the Fab build. Then read back what changed.
Blueprint graphsBlueprintTools builds graphs node by node (create_node, connect_pins, set_pin_value) and can fill a graph from an S-expression script with write_graph_dsl. Single calls apply as they come.Aethyr has the same node-level moves (add_node, wire_pins, set_pin_default). On top of them it adds apply_ops to land a whole graph in one call, preview_ops to check a batch first, compile_function to turn pseudocode into a wired function, and bp_structural_diff and recreate_blueprint. All of it works with no editor open.

The bridge doesn't fix everything. Bridged writes still skip Aethyr's compile gate and rollback. Bridged tools still need a live editor. If a job needs either, use Aethyr's native tools for it.

sections.heading: Where Epic leads
sections.html:
Aethyr isn't better at everything. The bridge exists because Epic's side is strong. Here's where Epic leads.

  • Zero install. Epic's plugin is a checkbox in any 5.8 editor. Aethyr is a plugin plus a server executable.
  • It grows with the engine. A new C++ function marked AICallable, or a new Python function decorated with tool_call, becomes a tool with no change to a separate server. Aethyr's tools are hand-written in its server.
  • Animation and cinematics. Epic's Sequencer and Control Rig toolsets are by far its largest area. Aethyr has a handful of Level Sequence tools and a few animation Blueprint tools.
  • Driving the live editor. Play In Editor, viewport capture, camera, selection, the content browser and the Slate UI all live in Epic's toolsets. Aethyr removed its own copies of those tools and sends the calls to Epic's.
  • Whole domains Aethyr has no native tool for. PCG, physics assets, MetaHuman, Chaos Cloth, MVVM, Dataflow, Data Registry and GAS cues are reachable only through the bridge.
  • Finer control over what's exposed. Epic's settings can block individual classes and properties from object property edits. Aethyr's allow and block lists (AETHYR_TOOL_ALLOW and AETHYR_TOOL_BLOCK) match on tool names only.

sections.heading: Every Epic toolset, side by side
sections.html:
Every toolset below comes from Epic's installed 5.8 plugins. Open one to see all of its functions. A table pairs each function with the closest Aethyr tool where one exists. Anything that couldn't be confirmed from source is left as no direct match. A missing pairing means no confirmed match.

  • Direct means the two do the same job.
  • Partial means they overlap. The note says how they differ.
  • Bridge only means Aethyr removed its own tool and sends you to Epic's. Aethyr's wiki page on the Engine Toolset Bridge has the full removed-tools table.

Names are the toolset class name without a C++ U prefix, then the function. You pass them to epic_call_tool as Toolset.Function. With enable_tool_category("epic"), Aethyr also offers one tool per function, with both parts lowercased. AssetTools.find_assets becomes epic_assettools_find_assets.

At time of writing, the plugins under Toolsets/ hold 56 toolset classes with 872 functions in all. Two more toolsets sit outside that folder, one in ToolsetRegistry and one in AIAssistant. They're listed last. Epic's MCPClientToolset plugin has no fixed functions. It mounts tools from an external MCP server that you configure in its settings.

Core editor control

The EditorToolset plugin. This is the one the bridge switches on by default.

sections.heading: What Aethyr has that Epic doesn't
sections.html:
These are the areas where Epic's toolsets have no function that does the same job, at time of writing. Some are Aethyr's depth in a shared area, such as Blueprints. Others are whole areas Epic doesn't cover.

AreaWhat Aethyr hasEpic side
Blueprint batchesapply_ops with atomic rollback, preview_ops dry runs, compile_function, bp_structural_diff, recreate_blueprint, clone_graph, implement_interface, find_dangling_references, find_overriders.Node-level tools and write_graph_dsl, with no batch preview, diff or rebuild function.
Blueprint data typescreate_struct, add_struct_member, create_enum, timelines (list_timelines, read_timeline).No matching function.
No-editor workReads and writes through the headless editor daemon, plus a mock backend with no engine.Needs a running editor.
AudioMetaSounds and Sound Cues, sound classes, attenuation and concurrency. The audio category has 26 tools at time of writing.No audio toolset.
Cook and packagecook_content, package_project.No matching function.
Diff and mergediff_asset, prepare_merge.No matching function.
Source control historyget_asset_history, load_asset_revision, unload_packages.AssetTools can tell you if an asset is checked out. Nothing reads history.
Profilingstart_profile, stop_profile, get_stats.No matching function.
Reflectionget_class_info, find_class, find_function, list_functions, get_struct_info, get_enum_info, get_interface_info.ObjectTools (search_subclasses, get_class, list_properties) covers part of it.
Node discoverylist_node_kinds, list_pin_categories, describe_k2node, describe_function_node, list_macro_library_functions.BlueprintTools has find_node_types and get_node_type_pins for the same question.
Editor state readersThe editor category (116 tools at time of writing) is mostly small get_* readers, such as get_blueprint_editor_state, get_outliner_state and get_cook_progress.Covers part of this through EditorAppToolset and SlateInspectorToolset.
Samplesinstall_samples builds sample Blueprints, data and UI that never overwrite your assets.None.

The full list of Aethyr tools by category is in the reference.

sections.heading: Which side to use for what
sections.html:
You don't have to choose. The skills Aethyr installs steer your AI to the right side. If you'd rather decide yourself, this is a good rule of thumb.

JobReach forWhy
Edit BlueprintsAethyrCompile checks, batches, backups and rollback. Works with no editor open.
Work with no editorAethyrThe headless editor serves reads and writes. Bridged Epic tools can't run there.
Run Play In EditorEpic, bridgedEditorAppToolset.StartPIE and StopPIE. Aethyr removed its own.
Capture the viewportEpic, bridgedEditorAppToolset.CaptureViewport adds optional annotations. take_screenshot is the simple option.
Drive the editor UIEpic, bridgedSlateInspectorToolset snapshots, clicks and types.
Animate with SequencerEpic, bridgedFar more functions. Use Aethyr's Level Sequence tools for basic authoring.
Build Niagara effectsEitherAethyr's tools are compile-gated and add module script graphs. Epic adds schemas and stack-issue fixes.
Use PCG or physicsEpic, bridgedAethyr has no native tool for these.
Author audioAethyrEpic has no audio toolset.
Ship a buildAethyrCook and package, plus diff, merge and asset history.
Settings and pluginsEitherBoth list and change project settings, plugins, Game Features and Gameplay Tags.

Using Epic's side. Today the optional plugin dependency turns on EditorToolset when your project has its own editor target. Blueprint-only precompiled projects start the editor with Saved/Aethyr/Launch-Editor.bat. For more toolsets, run AethyrMcp.exe launch-editor --epic-toolsets all. Set AETHYR_EPIC_INTEROP=0 to turn the bridge off.
